learning_objective: 🎯 You will learn the traffic signals of writing! Discover how capital letters and punctuation marks give your sentences clear meaning and emotion.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Always use a capital letter for the first word of a sentence, the word 'I', and special Proper Nouns like names of people, places, days, and months!
Every sentence needs a stop sign! Use a full stop (.) for facts and commands, a question mark (?) for asking things, and an exclamation mark (!) for strong feelings.
A comma tells the reader to take a tiny pause. We use it to separate items in a list (like apples, bananas, and grapes) or to separate parts of a long sentence.
The apostrophe has two jobs! It shows that someone owns something (Rahul's book), or it takes the place of missing letters in short words called contractions (do not becomes don't).

fun_activity.title: ✍️ The Punctuation Rescue Mission
fun_activity.instructions: Take this messy sentence: 'wow my friend rohan loves pizza burgers and cake' and rewrite it with the correct capital letters and punctuation marks!

quick_recap: ⭐ Capitalize the first word of every sentence, the letter 'I', and all Proper Nouns.
⭐ End sentences with a full stop, question mark, or exclamation mark.
⭐ Use a comma to separate items in a list or to pause.
⭐ Use an apostrophe to show ownership or to make contractions.
